title: IOS Files and Backups: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: A router has a filing cabinet and a notepad. One survives a power cut. The other doesn't.

lines.t: A filing cabinet and a notepad

scenes.heading: The cabinet and notepad
scenes.narration: Where things live decides whether they survive. Flash holds the I O S image, and it survives a reboot. N V R A M holds the startup config, and it survives too. R A M holds the running config, and a reboot wipes it. So always copy running config to startup config.

scenes.heading: Commands
scenes.narration: Three commands to remember. List what's in flash. Save your changes. And see what will survive a reboot.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. Startup config is in N V R A M. You have to save it yourself. Delete just marks the file.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva IOS files lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Running is in R A M, and startup is in N V R A M. Always copy run start. Flash holds the I O S image. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva IOS files lab.
